data.narrative:
Synchron is a Series D biotech company that has raised $200M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public companies (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private firms in the Biotech & Health sector, with particular focus on same-stage comparables including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B Series C), Chai Discovery ($3.8B Series C), and New Limit ($3.1B Series C).

Two methods proved applicable to triangulation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $200M total-raised proxy, implying a $300M valuation. Peer-median analysis draws on the three same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables listed above, which span a $3.1B–$10.3B range with a median of $3.8B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples could not be applied, as Synchron does not disclose revenue figures typical of private companies.

The two applicable methods produce a wide triangulated range: $255M (low), $2.0B (median), and $4.4B (high). The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects the early-stage nature of the company relative to later-stage peers. Key uncertainties include the relevance of Series C comparables to a Series D context, the wide dispersion in peer valuations (3.3x from min to max), and the absence of revenue data to calibrate public-company multiples. A Series D valuation is most defensible in the $2B–$4B band pending disclosure of capital deployment metrics.
